scenario.description: An HR business partner must decide whether to approve Nadia's requested transfer from Product Operations to Customer Enablement and finalize the transfer date, temporary workload, communication boundary, onboarding support, and handoff requirements.

shared_context.S1: Nadia has requested an internal transfer from Product Operations to an open role in Customer Enablement after a difficult working relationship on her current team.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding decision on whether the transfer proceeds and what safeguards accompany it.
shared_context.S3: The receiving role is available, and Nadia's current team needs a documented handoff before the move is complete.
shared_context.S4: The transfer review policy requires documented input from the employee, the current team, the receiving manager, and Employee Relations before approval; Marcus is the current-team representative for this review.
shared_context.S5: Elena's routine review checklist requires each of those four representatives to make a separate formal disclosure entry for their input, and Elena does not finalize the review until all four entries are recorded.

PF1.text: Nadia told the recruiting coordinator that she can accept the transfer only if it starts on 2025-01-06 and her Customer Enablement workload is limited to exactly 80 percent for her first four weeks; those conditions were not copied into the formal request.

PF2.text: Marcus personally witnessed exactly two occasions when Nadia and her current project lead exchanged hostile messages, and Nadia's safe working arrangement requires no direct one-to-one contact with that project lead after the transfer; Marcus has not put his observations in a formal incident record.

PF3.text: Priyanka's role assessment found that Nadia needs exactly three weeks of paired shadowing on customer-escalation cases before handling them independently, and Priyanka is prepared to provide that shadowing; the assessment remains in the receiving team's working notes.

PF4.text: Theo confirmed that this transfer requires a written handoff lasting exactly 10 business days and a documented nonretaliation check before closure; he verified the requirement with Employee Relations this week, but the guidance has not yet been added to the transfer template.

interaction_config.formal_disclosure_requirement: Before Elena may settle, A2, A3, A4, and A5 must each make a dedicated reveal action for their formal review input; an ordinary say turn does not satisfy that checklist entry.

acceptance_conditions: Nadia's initial workload must be exactly 80 percent for four weeks.
Nadia must have no direct one-to-one contact with her current project lead after the transfer.
The receiving team must provide exactly three weeks of paired shadowing.
The handoff must last exactly 10 business days.
A nonretaliation check must be documented before closure.
The settlement must explicitly use the four private facts spoken by their owners.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF4' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Nadia's stated conditions change the transfer start date to exactly 2025-01-06 and the initial workload to exactly 80 percent.
The two witnessed hostile exchanges and Nadia's required boundary change direct contact with the project lead from ordinary contact to prohibited one-to-one contact.
The receiving team's role assessment changes onboarding from unspecified support to exactly three weeks of paired shadowing for Nadia.
The verified Employee Relations guidance changes the handoff to exactly 10 business days and requires a documented nonretaliation check before closure.
